facts.statement: Bashanosaurus is an extinct stegosaurian dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic of China.
facts.quote: Bashanosaurus (meaning "Bashan lizard") is an extinct genus of stegosaurian dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic (Bathonian age) Shaximiao Formation of Yunyang County, China.

facts.statement: The genus Bashanosaurus contains only one species, Bashanosaurus primitivus, known from three incomplete skeletons.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Bashanosaurus primitivus, known from incomplete skeletons belonging to three individuals.

facts.statement: Fossils of Bashanosaurus were found in a quarry discovered in 2016 in Chongqing, China.
facts.quote: In 2016, a quarry of dinosaur fossils representing outcrops of the lower Shaximiao Formation was found in Laojun Village of Pu'an Township in Yunyang County, Chongqing Municipality, China.

facts.statement: The name Bashanosaurus combines the ancient name for Chongqing with the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name, "'Bashanosaurus", combines "Bashan"—the ancient name of Chongqing, where the fossils were discovered—with the Greek "sauros", meaning "lizard".

facts.statement: Bashanosaurus lived during the Bathonian age of the Middle Jurassic, with a maximum age of 166.0±1.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Bashanosaurus is notable for a stegosaur because of its early age, having been found in rocks dating to the Bathonian age (maximum age of 166.0±1.5 Ma) of the Middle Jurassic epoch.

facts.statement: Bashanosaurus is the oldest named stegosaur known from Asia.
facts.quote: This makes it the oldest named stegosaur known from Asia.

facts.statement: Bashanosaurus was a quadrupedal herbivore with a row of plates and spines running from its neck to its tail.
facts.quote: As a stegosaur, Bashanosaurus would have been a quadrupedal herbivore with a paired row of a combination of large plates and spines running along the top of the animal from the neck to the tail tip.

facts.statement: The tail armor of Bashanosaurus likely served as a defensive structure against predators.
facts.quote: These armor pieces—especially those on the end of the tail—could have served as defensive structures against predators.

facts.statement: Seven dorsal vertebrae are known from Bashanosaurus.
facts.quote: In total, seven dorsal vertebrae are known from Bashanosaurus.

facts.statement: The centra of Bashanosaurus dorsal vertebrae are flat on both ends.
facts.quote: The centrum of this bone is amphiplatyan, meaning that it is flat on both ends.

facts.statement: Bashanosaurus had a poorly developed acromial process on its scapula.
facts.quote: The acromial process of the scapula is unusual, being poorly developed.

facts.statement: The fourth trochanter of the Bashanosaurus femur is uniquely positioned below the middle of the shaft.
facts.quote: The fourth trochanter of the femur is incomplete, but visible as a ridge with a distinct process. It is unique in being positioned below the middle of the shaft of the femur, rather than at the midpoint, as in other stegosaurs.

facts.statement: Four incomplete osteoderms, consisting of one spine and three plates, are known from Bashanosaurus.
facts.quote: Four incomplete osteodermss are known from Bashanosaurus, consisting of one spine and three plates.

facts.statement: The specific morphology of Bashanosaurus dermal plates is considered a unique trait of the species.
facts.quote: This dermal plate morphology is considered to be an autapomorphy of Bashanosaurus.

facts.statement: Bashanosaurus fossils show a unique mix of features typically found in both adult and immature animals.
facts.quote: The fossil material of Bashanosaurus demonstrates a unique blend of features typically seen in both adult and immature animals.

facts.statement: Researchers estimate Bashanosaurus may have been about 3 meters long based on comparisons with Huayangosaurus.
facts.quote: Based on the proportions of Huayangosaurus, Dai et al. (2022) estimate that Bashanosaurus may have been about 3 m long.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the known Bashanosaurus specimens were fully grown, suggesting the animal may have been capable of growing larger.
facts.quote: However, it is unclear if the fossil specimens belonged to fully grown animals, so it may have been able to grow larger.

facts.statement: Dai and colleagues (2022) classified Bashanosaurus as the most basal member of the Stegosauria, placing it as the sister taxon to Chungkingosaurus.
facts.quote: In their 2022 description of Bashanosaurus, Dai and colleagues recovered it in the basalmost clade within the Stegosauria, as the sister taxon to the Late Jurassic Chungkingosaurus.

facts.statement: A 2025 study by Sánchez-Fenollosa and Cobos placed Bashanosaurus within the Huayangosauridae clade as the sister taxon to Huayangosaurus.
facts.quote: Sánchez-Fenollosa and Cobos (2025) recovered Bashanosaurus as a member of a larger Huayangosauridae clade, as the sister taxon to Huayangosaurus.

facts.statement: The genus Bashanosaurus was named by Dai and colleagues in 2022.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Dai et al., 2022

facts.statement: The species Bashanosaurus primitivus was named by Dai and colleagues in 2022.
facts.quote: species_authority: Dai et al., 2022

facts.statement: Bashanosaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 169 million years ago in the Bajocian age.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 169 millones de años, en el Bajociense

facts.statement: The time range for Bashanosaurus is estimated from 168.2 to 161.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Callovian (168.2 to 161.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Bashanosaurus were recovered from the Shaximiao Formation in Yunyang, Chongqing, China.
facts.quote: Se ha recuperado de la Formación Shaximiao de Yunyang, Chongqing, China.

facts.statement: The fossil material was discovered in a quarry in Chongqing in 2016.
facts.quote: El material se recuperó de una cantera en Chongqing descubierta en 2016

facts.statement: The specimens were named Bashanosaurus primitivus in a 2022 article.
facts.quote: Los especímenes recibieron el nombre de Bashanosaurus primitivus en un artículo de 2022

facts.statement: Bashanosaurus primitivus is the only known species of the extinct genus Bashanosaurus, a basal stegosaurian dinosaur.
facts.quote: Bashanosaurus primitivus ("Lagarto de Bashan primitivo") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Bashanosaurus de dinosaurio tireóforo estegosauriano

facts.statement: Descriptores estimate the holotype measured 2.8 meters in length, though it may have grown larger as the specimens are subadults.
facts.quote: Sus descriptores estiman que el holotipo medía 2,8 metros de largo, pero dado que los especímenes son subadultos puede haber crecido más.

facts.statement: Bashanosaurus is known from two partial skeletons and a vertebra from a third individual.
facts.quote: Bashanosaurus se conoce a partir de dos esqueletos parciales, junto con una vértebra que proviene de un tercer individuo.

facts.statement: The holotype includes limb bones, back and tail vertebrae, plates, and a spike.
facts.quote: El holotipo, CLGPR V00006-1, incluye huesos de las extremidades, vértebras de la espalda y la cola, placas y una espiga.

facts.statement: Several characteristics of Bashanosaurus resemble the basal thyreophore Scelidosaurus.
facts.quote: Varias de sus características recuerdan al tireóforo basal Scelidosaurus

facts.statement: Bashanosaurus is one of the most basal stegosaurs and is the oldest known stegosaur, replacing Adratiklit as the oldest known species.
facts.quote: Es uno de los estegosaurios más basales y también es el estegosaurio más antiguo conocido, reemplazando al estegosaurio más antiguo conocido, Adratiklit, que es aproximadamente un millón de años más joven.

facts.statement: Bashanosaurus lived in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: en lo que es hoy Asia

facts.statement: Bashanosaurus fossils were found in the "Dinosaur Fossil Wall" locality of the Lower Member of the Shaximiao Formation in Yunyang County, China, dating to the Bathonian age of the Middle Jurassic.
facts.quote: The Bashanosaurus fossil material was discovered in the "Dinosaur Fossil Wall" locality of the Shaximiao Formation (Lower Member) of Yunyang County, China, which dates to the Bathonian age of the Middle Jurassic.

facts.statement: The bonebed containing Bashanosaurus fossils also yielded sauropods such as Omeisaurus puxiani, Shunosaurus, and Yuzhoulong.
facts.quote: Several other dinosaur fossils, predominantly belonging to sauropods, have also been found in this bonebed, including Omeisaurus puxiani (a mamenchisaurid), Shunosaurus (a basal eusauropod), and Yuzhoulong (a basal macronarian).

facts.statement: The non-dinosaurian fauna at the site included pterosaurs, turtles, crocodyliforms, pliosaurid plesiosaurs, therapsids, fish, and amphibians.
facts.quote: The non-dinosaurian fauna includes pterosaurs (Angustinaripterus), turtles (Chengyuchelys spp., Plesiochelys, and Trionyx), crocodyliforms (Teleosaurus, Sunosuchus, and Hsisosuchus), pliosaurid plesiosaurs, therapsids (Bienotheroides and Polistodon), fish (Hybodus, Yuchoulepis, Lepidotes, and Ceratodus), and amphibians (Sinobrachyops).

facts.statement: It is debated whether later phylogenetic analyses confirm the exact placement of Bashanosaurus, though results have been very similar to the original description.
facts.quote: Later publications built upon this phylogenetic dataset and found very similar results to the original description.

rejected.statement: Hui Dai and colleagues described Bashanosaurus primitivus as a new genus and species in 2022.
rejected.quote: In 2022, Hui Dai and colleagues described Bashanosaurus primitivus as a new genus and species of basal stegosaurian based on these fossil remains.
